results_numeric.quantity: Clump masses R1, R2, R3 (Tex=50 K)

findings_qualitative.value: Blue and red lobes differ strongly in size and morphology

evidence.quote: The most striking aspect of this outflow is the clear difference in size and morphology between the two different lobes

findings_qualitative.value: Velocity gradients across the cavity are inconsistent with rotation

evidence.quote: Yet, we are certain it is not consistent with outflow rotation.

claims.hypothesis: Is the blue lobe entrained by a wide-angle wind?
claims.experiment: Fit parabolic shell model to integrated map and p-v diagram
claims.result: C=0.3±0.05, v_o=2.3±0.2, i=29±1 deg give reasonable fits
claims.finding: Blue lobe consistent with wide-angle wind entrainment, coexisting with a jet

evidence.quote: suggests that the observed blue lobe could very likely have been formed by the entrainment of a wide-angle wind and the ambient cloud

claims.hypothesis: Do the red clumps trace episodic ejections?
claims.experiment: Clump spacing and p-v Hubble wedges
claims.result: Three clumps at ~0.1 pc spacing with ages 360-945 yr
claims.finding: Bow-shock entrainment by episodes every few hundred years

evidence.quote: This suggests they might be the result of periodic ejection episodes

claims.hypothesis: Does higher sensitivity raise outflow energetics?
claims.experiment: Measured mass, momentum, energy over >3σ velocity range
claims.result: Emission to -30 and 40 km/s; higher momentum and energy than Olberg et al.
claims.finding: Outflows may be more energetic than previously thought

evidence.quote: results in significantly higher values of the outflow kinetic energy and momentum

claims.hypothesis: Does cavity velocity gradient indicate rotation?

evidence.quote: Undoubtedly, the detected gradient is not due to outflow rotation

why_this_data.value: High-resolution observations needed to study entrainment, wind and outflow properties

evidence.quote: The high resolution data were obtained with the aim of studying the entrainment process, the underlying protostellar wind and the properties of the molecular outflow.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Jet precession alone cannot produce the wide cavity

evidence.quote: It is therefore highly unlikely that precession of the jet alone could, by itself, produce the wide-angle cavity traced by the CO outflow.

limitations_admitted.value: Masses are lower limits (optically thin, Tex uncertain, missing large-scale flux)

evidence.quote: We thus estimate the mass assuming the line is optically thin, and warn that our masses are very likely underestimated, by a factor of few or even as much as an order of magnitude

referee_caveats_inferred: Tex range spans a factor of ~5 in mass/energy
